S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is defined by marked, out-of-proportion fear of a particular object or situation that reliably triggers immediate anxiety and leads to avoidance or fearful endurance. It is typically circumscribed rather than broad or free-floating, and is distinguished from panic disorder or generalized anxiety by the predictable link to a specific phobic cue and by impairment tied to avoiding that cue.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient.stressor: Two years ago, Lindell Alvarez moved into an older Norfolk apartment building undergoing piecemeal repairs, where repeated plumbing work and gaps around the laundry room made rodent sightings a recurring topic among tenants. Although Lindell had always been meticulous about cleanliness, this change in living condition became the setting in which a strong, out-of-proportion fear of rats took hold and began to generalize to basements, utility rooms, alley trash areas, and older commercial buildings. Across 2 years and 0 months, the fear became severely impairing because Lindell declined cleaning routes that involved storage areas, delayed jobs when signs of pests were mentioned, and sometimes could only complete assignments by enduring them with intense fear, threatening their reputation for reliability and future supervisory prospects. Psychiatric care began after Lindell requested a formal workplace accommodation and occupational health referred them for evaluation because the avoidance was no longer manageable within normal route scheduling.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: I’m here because the thought of seeing a rat has gotten so bad that I can’t do parts of my cleaning job anymore, even when I know it’s probably just an old building or a trash room and not really dangerous.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If I hear scratching near a wall or see something move by a pipe, my whole body reacts right away—my heart pounds, my hands shake, and I feel like I have to get out before I can even think straight.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I turn down routes with basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, or alley dumpsters when I can, and if I’m forced to clean one I keep the door open, rush through it, and feel scared the whole time.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve had to refuse or delay cleaning assignments in certain buildings, and my supervisor has started questioning whether I can be counted on for regular routes. I’m worried this will cost me better shifts or a chance at a lead position.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about two years, since I moved into the older apartment building where people kept talking about rats.
